name: NatureScapes
line: Two to five days in forest, mountain, desert or mangrove.
deck: Six destinations, four ecosystems, one school group at a time. None of the six explains itself from a classroom, which is the only reason to take a bus that far.
geography: Sariska · Ranthambore · Mukteshwar, Sirmaur · Jim Corbett · Sunderbans · Jaisalmer

aims.h: Let the place set the length
aims.p: Two days to five, decided by the destination rather than by a calendar. A programme that runs to one fixed length is selling logistics.
There is a day of work in this on purpose. Without it the whole thing is a viewing, and viewings do not change what anybody does afterwards.

aims.h: Build a comparison, not a trip
aims.p: The four ecosystems exist so a school can hold one against another. One journey is an outing; two are an argument.
The intent is a class rather than an assortment of individuals, because a week only lands if everybody goes back to the same corridor.

how.p: Two days to five. A day in the Sunderbans is a boat day; a day at Jaisalmer is a heat day. The programme does not pretend those are the same trip and does not price them as one.
It is the school journeys programme, so a cohort arrives from one school already knowing each other — which means the week has somewhere to land when everyone gets back to the same corridor.
The four ecosystems are the spine of the programme, and the destinations hang off them. A group that has done two of the four has something to compare, which is when the learning starts.

activities.name: Ecosystem learning
activities.p: The reason for the distance. Two days to five inside one ecosystem, learning the part of it that only holds together on site.
activities.cap: Langurs, on one of our own journeys.

frame.alt: A family of langurs resting along a fallen branch

activities.name: Community interaction
activities.p: The people who live where the journey goes. A destination with nobody in it is a landscape rather than a place.

frame.alt: A large group seated on a hillside slope

activities.name: Shramdaan
activities.p: A day of physical work. Nobody expects it in a nature programme, and it is the day most groups talk about on the way home.

activities.name: Self development
activities.p: Writing, observation and time alone, built into the week rather than left to happen in the gaps.

frame.alt: A group spread across a hillside writing and observing under a tree

who.p: Whole classes rather than individuals. This is the school journeys programme and the group is the unit.

who.h: Students who have been to none of the four
who.p: Forest, Himalayan, desert, marine. A photograph of a mangrove has never once told anybody what standing in one is like.
Somebody from the school is on every journey, and what they carry back into a classroom is the part of this we never see.

done.p: Over sixty journeys, for schools including the Shriram Schools and Modern Schools.

holes.what: Every frame on this page is ours and not one of them is of the six destinations. The only pictures we hold of those were bought from a stock library, and this page will not use them.
holes.unlocks: Any Swechha frames from the sixty-plus journeys. One per ecosystem would let this page open on its own work.

holes.what: Sariska is on the destination list and on nothing else we hold — no photograph, no account, no journal.
holes.unlocks: Confirmation that Sariska is still a destination.

holes.what: No start year is published, so sixty journeys is a total and not a rate.

statement.line: The ecosystem sets the length, not us.
statement.under: A boat day and a heat day are not the same day.
